implementerProof.how: Re-ran proofs 1-3 independently. Proof 1/2: `cd packages/envoy && BROKER_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:54487/postgres?sslmode=disable go test -count=1 -v -run TestABrokerOutageLongerThanALease ./cmd/broker` at 58df5554: --- PASS (87.20s), 0 SKIP, survivor fetch served 87ms after restart, renewer renewed to 44.922s 5.978s after restart, broker logged 'gave back ... gap=58.338365s ... enrollments=2'. Negative control: a fresh `git archive eee1605637ff packages/envoy` export with this outage_test.go, GOWORK=off: --- FAIL (79.01s) on 'agent-secrets: proof invalid: not live (PROOF_INVALID)', 0 SKIP. Proof 3: `go test -count=1 -v ./internal/broker/enroll ./internal/broker/api ./internal/broker/requests ./internal/broker/config` all ok, 383 PASS, 0 SKIP. Proof 4 is rejected: its surface (an httptest broker that closes the connection with no answer) is not what the daemon meets in either outage the plan defines. In production the daemon's agent_secrets url is the broker's HTTPS front door (the deployment repository's legion stack sets agentSecretsUrl to the broker's front door, a Tailscale serve HTTPS proxy to the broker's Service), whose proxy is httputil.ReverseProxy with no ErrorHandler (tailscale ipn/ipnlocal/serve.go:982), so it answers 502 while no broker serves; and the real broker binary answers a valid token login 500 INTERNAL while its database is away (observed). Both are HTTP answers, so the login stays on the 30 s to 5 min schedule, and the criterion 'logs in again within about 10 s' fails there.

failures.criterion: The daemon logs in again within about 10 s of the broker answering (plan acceptance 5; PR body: 'after an outage, new pods can enroll within about 10 s instead of up to 5 min')
failures.evidence: Red tests committed in 8502875f, packages/daemon/internal/agentsecrets/client_test.go: TestTokenLoginRetriesQuicklyWhileTheFrontDoorAnswersForADownBroker (a real httputil.ReverseProxy, as Tailscale serve runs it, in front of a dead port answers the first 3 logins 502, then forwards to the fake broker) and TestTokenLoginRetriesQuicklyWhileTheBrokerCannotReachItsDatabase (the broker answers 3 logins 500 {"code":"INTERNAL","error":"token login failed"}, the exact answer the real broker binary gave a valid token login with its Postgres stopped). `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 -run TestTokenLoginRetries -v ./internal/agentsecrets` at 8502875f: both FAIL 'timed out waiting: a login to succeed ... well before a refusal's minute' (5.01s each); the implementer's two tests still PASS. With the refusal schedule shortened to 20ms the same front-door rig passes in 0.19s, so the red is the 502/500 classification alone. Fix direction: a login answered 5xx (no decision about the token) takes the short schedule, as an unanswered one does; 4xx keeps the long one.
